summary: Ordinary invoke/stream/readiness share one HTTP transport; extraction uses a fixed pure data client tool with server-side native denial proven on a pinned local Gateway; cron accepts only exact job/run completion within one deadline.

operator_clarification.scope: A pinned reproducible local/dev Gateway with a synthetic model or no-auth test route may satisfy functional acceptance. No real account credentials or authenticated external Gateway required. Tool/tenant safety and 100-request CLI/HTTP benchmark remain required.

changes: Removed ordinary CLI invocation, argv size routing, and the unused CLI reply decoder; administrative cron/auth CLI and read-only kernel delegation retained.
One HTTP builder preserves admitted agent/model, scoped session, messages/context/attachments, trace, errors, usage, and terminal outcome.
Readiness no longer falls back to another model; a previous explicit override cannot change subsequent ordinary routing.
Restricted emit_extraction schema and argument validation reject invalid or unexpected tools; native tools are separately denied in the pinned Gateway fixture.

Cron uses exact id/runId lookup and requires both jobId and runId in the returned entry. Missing run ID, late results, failed/cancelled/skipped runs and real hung subprocess fail without resubmission.
Fixed test_cron.py canonical package imports so the previously excluded cron suite now runs.

P1 correction: invoke and stream share conversation resolution: internal explicit session ID, metadata.session_user, then legacy metadata.session_id. Tenant/actor escaping and positional identity remain unchanged.

P2 correction: one effective-model resolver is used by invoke, stream and readiness. Main-agent defaults resolve to OPENCLAW_PRIMARY_MODEL/provider default; non-default agents retain their Gateway model unless an admitted explicit override is supplied.

Mounted HTTP regressions prove conversation continuity/isolation, session alias precedence, identical default model headers including readiness, and preservation of admitted explicit/agent-configured models.
implementation.post_measurement_change: None: the replay measures the exact final provider bytes. Subsequent changes are test/docs/evidence and conflict-free dev merges of development tooling and Registry/BFF owner work; no task-owned transport or cron files changed.

manifest.auth_route: isolated loopback Gateway, synthetic test token; local deterministic OpenAI-completions model
manifest.session_design: 10 independent admitted agents, each with 10 sequential turns per arm; first is session-cold, next 9 warm; four concurrent sequences, one shared Gateway, no process-cold claim
manifest.usage_semantics: model fixture reports fixed input=100/output=10/total=110, not a tokenizer or production cost measurement
manifest.ttft_semantics: CLI buffered invoke first text available on return; HTTP first normalized delta; full includes invocation and normalization
manifest.latency_limitation: CLI transport includes docker exec overhead; local fixture measures transport and Gateway, not external model quality or latency

limitations: Synthetic model usage is fixed fixture accounting, not real tokenizer usage or model billing. No production model quality, cost, or latency claim.
Four legacy real-account smoke tests remain skipped; the required pinned local Gateway capabilities and benchmark were executed separately, not inferred from those skips.
Cold means first turn in a new agent session; process startup is prewarmed by capability checks. CLI TTFT is text availability at buffered invoke return, and includes Docker exec overhead.
Hosted services/configuration were not changed or accepted. Hosted extraction needs the same Gateway-side native deny policy; client tool_choice alone is not a sandbox.
Other shared host work can influence wall-clock timings; CPU quota was unavailable.
The production Docker cron transport integrations/openclaw/adapter/cron_transport.py remains outside this task artifact grant and still needs an owner scope handoff for its most-recent-run fallback.
